title: Sequential model-based optimization discovers two previously unreported chemical reactions
summary: A programmable robotic synthesis platform used inline HPLC, Raman or NMR feedback and closed-loop optimization to explore selected reaction spaces. In a tosMIC campaign, sequential model-based optimization with a Gaussian-process surrogate identified a reaction between toluenesulphonylmethyl isocyanide and benzylidenemalononitrile; subsequent optimization increased yield from the 27% initial condition to 49% (22 percentage points) over 50 reactions. The article also reports a second previously unreported reaction and an exploratory trifluoromethylation campaign that discovered new molecules.
ai_technology: ChemputationOptimizer, a sensor-integrated reaction engine with sequential model-based optimization (Gaussian-process surrogate); the platform also exposes random search, design-of-experiments, Bayesian-optimization and genetic-algorithm routines

evidence.tested: The article also reports a second previously unreported reaction and an exploratory trifluoromethylation campaign that discovered new molecules.
evidence.unknown: The platform's reported yield gains are specific to these selected reaction spaces and objectives, not general chemistry performance. The tosMIC and phloroglucinol campaigns are reported as previously unreported reactions; product characterization and complete procedure details are in the article/supplement. The system includes several optimization algorithms and the authors note random search can be a strong baseline; the reported tosMIC optimization used SMBO with a Gaussian-process surrogate. No claim is made that the reactions are industrially useful or broadly generalizable. Primary source checked; no independent replication assessed.
evidence.ai_role: For the tosMIC and phloroglucinol explorations, machine-guided combinatorial search proposed reaction parameters and inline spectroscopic feedback supplied product-yield measurements; a Gaussian-process sequential-model-based optimizer guided the reaction-space exploration and follow-up optimization. Human chemists defined reaction space and experimental constraints, and performed/characterized the experiments.
